_about: The requirements vendors respond to (STORY-012, REQ-022). Copied from the requirement list in the STORY-000 brief, because the published plan.json has no requirements yet. tests/vendorSubmissions.test.js checks this list has exactly the requirement ids the plan's stories reference. Replace it with the plan's requirements once the platform republishes them.

requirements.statement: The system must provide a work order management system for Herriman City.
The system must be a work order management system.
Vendors must indicate compliance and technical approach for each requirement outlined.
The system must support bidirectional GIS integration to select assets and autofill multiple fields into a work order.
The system must actively read from and write to the primary GIS database.
The system must possess spatial analysis capabilities to generate heat maps based on work order types and geographical frequency.
The system must provide an additional freeform location text field for use if specific location information is missing from the GIS database.
The system must provide a public-facing reporting interface allowing citizens to submit requests or view public work order activities.
The system must natively interface or provide verified API connections to core systems.
The system must provide the ability to update, complete, and respond to Bluestakes data within the platform.
The system must provide fully open database or API compatibility allowing Madison AI engines to index, crawl, and search internal work order data.
The system must comply with existing workflows and accommodate new workflows.
The system must enable system administrators to manage user access, configurations, and audits.
The system must allow for successful creation, updating, and completion of work orders, as evidenced by user testing and demonstration.
Time must be allotted for configuring, testing, and data conversion.
The software must be operational by July 1, 2027.
API specifications and testing must be coordinated with specific vendors.
The system must provide API interfaces for Lama, Sprypoint, and Madison AI.
